desc: Derive and prove the reduction: answer = min over feasible levels L of |Y−L|+|Z−L|; closed form via T = maximin connectivity level (|Y−Z| if T ≥ min(Y,Z), else Y+Z−2T). Verified on samples (10 and 2).

Implement the max-spanning-tree + binary-lifting solution: edges weight=min(F_u,F_v), Kruskal descending, iterative DFS for depth/parent, tables as array('i') (19 levels), per-query bottleneck in O(log N).
Implement DSU (path compression + union by size) for Kruskal; node id = i*W+j.
Compute final answer per query from T with the closed form; handle s==t separately (answer |Y−Z|).
Write fast input parsing (sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()) for ~1.5M ints; output Q lines.

Validate on hand-made cases: uniform F grid, H=1/W=1 path graphs, Y=Z, adjacent blocks, and the provided samples (expect 10 and 2); audit packing (PACK=1<<20 vs w ≤ 1e6), LOG sufficiency, root INF sentinel, memory (~38MB) and speed (~8M ops for queries, ~5M for table build).
